R001.fact: In a finite-dimensional vector space W over a field, a linearly independent family indexed by a finite set J with |J|=dim W is a basis.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space of finite dimension λ+1.
F001 gives |I|=n=λ+1.

R001.justification: The elementary exchange argument bounds the size of any independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: insert independent vectors successively into a spanning list, each time replacing a vector with nonzero coefficient in an expansion, preserving spanning. If an independent family of size dim W did not span, adjoining a vector outside its span would give an independent family of size dim W+1, contradicting that bound applied to a basis of W. Thus the given family spans and is a basis.

R001.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m!/(r!(m−r)!) is an integer, denoted binom(m,r). Consequently, for integers a≥0 and r≥0, (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer, with empty product 1.

i∈I means 0≤i≤λ, so both a=λ−i and a=i are nonnegative integers.
r is an arbitrary natural number.
The two computed successive products use a=λ−i and a=i, respectively.

R001.justification: The factorial quotients equal 1 at r=0 and r=m. For 0<r<m, direct common-denominator arithmetic gives C(m,r)=C(m−1,r−1)+C(m−1,r). Induction on m therefore proves every such quotient integral. Cancelling a! in (a+r)!/a! gives the stated successive-product expression. Interpreting these integers in ℂ gives exactly the coefficients in S005; all factorial denominators are nonzero.

R002.fact: If (m_i) indexed by the finite set I is an integer basis of M and also a complex basis of V, then R⊗_ℤ M has R-basis (1⊗m_i). The map r⊗m↦rm into V is injective, has image the R-span of M, and its image spans V over ℂ. Here |I|=n, so its R-rank is n.

grounds.reason: H005 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V.
N001 supplies the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I and |I|=n, so finite-dimensional basis cardinality gives the same indexing size for m.
R is a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ under H001.
M_R is the stated tensor product.
iota is the canonical scalar-multiplication map.

R002.justification: Finite basis exchange gives equality of the cardinalities of the two complex bases. Write a_i:M→ℤ for the integer coordinate maps for m. The maps r⊗m↦r a_i(m) are well-defined by bilinearity and give an inverse to (r_i)↦∑r_i⊗m_i. The map into V sends this sum to ∑r_i m_i, which vanishes only if every coefficient vanishes, by complex independence and R⊂ℂ. Its image is precisely the finite R-linear combinations of M, contains each m_i, and hence has complex span V. This elaborates the coordinate construction already displayed in S001.

R002.fact: For a prime p and integers 0≤j≤λ<p, the integer c=binom(λ,j) is not divisible by p and is a unit in R=ℤ_(p), with inverse 1/c∈R.

grounds.reason: p is prime.
j∈I means 0≤j≤λ.
A rational with denominator not divisible by p belongs to R.

R002.justification: Each positive factor in these factorials is less than p and therefore coprime to p; the Euclidean algorithm gives an inverse for its residue modulo p. Products of these invertible residues remain invertible, including the empty product 1. Thus p does not divide λ!. If p divided c, the displayed integer identity would force p to divide λ!, a contradiction. Consequently c≠0 and the fraction 1/c satisfies the defining denominator condition for R; its product with c is 1.

R003.justification: Choose a finite basis b_1,…,b_n of M_R from its finite freeness. Their images generate L. By R-linearity, E_ii(∑ r_a iota(b_a))=∑ r_a E_ii(iota(b_a)), so these finitely many projected images generate J e_i. Scalar multiplication J→J e_i is surjective by the definition of J e_i and injective since e_i≠0 in a complex vector space. Transporting the projected generators through its inverse yields a finite generating family of J.

R004.fact: For R=ℤ_(p)⊂ℚ and an R-submodule J⊂ℂ, every element of ℚ⊗_R J has the form d⁻¹⊗c with 0≠d∈R and c∈J. Multiplication is a well-defined injective ℚ-linear map with image span_ℚ(J). If J is finitely generated over R, the images of those generators span the tensor product over ℚ.

R004.justification: For a finite sum ∑ρ_j⊗c_j choose a common nonzero integer denominator d and integers a_j=dρ_j. Balancing gives ∑ρ_j⊗c_j=d⁻¹⊗∑a_jc_j. Multiplication is balanced because the R actions are scalar multiplication in ℂ. If its image is zero, c/d=0 in ℂ forces c=0. Its image consists precisely of rational linear combinations, and an R-generating expression for c gives the asserted finite rational spanning set.

R004.justification: After using that coordinate isomorphism, project each pure tensor to its component tensors. For the inverse, apply the tensor of each coordinate insertion to the corresponding tensor component and sum over finite I. The maps exist by balancing. Projection followed by insertion is the identity on the corresponding component and zero on all others; the sum of insertion-projection maps is the identity on the finite product. Checking on pure tensors therefore proves both compositions are identities. No exactness or flatness theorem is involved.

R004.fact: The rings R=ℤ_(p) and ℚ satisfy the strong rank condition. A finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space is free and finitely generated; finite dimension is invariant under linear isomorphism. A finite free R-module of rank n has natural finrank n, so the finite-rank uses of M001 and M002 here measure the ordinary dimensions appearing in S002.

R004.justification: A finite rational spanning set yields a basis by successively removing dependent vectors. Gaussian elimination shows an independent family in ℚ^t has size at most t, proving strong rank for ℚ and invariance of finite basis size. If an injective matrix R^s→R^t had a nonzero rational kernel vector, multiplying it by a common nonzero integer denominator would give a nonzero kernel vector in R^s. Its rational extension is thus injective, so s≤t. This proves strong rank for R; comparison of finite bases consequently identifies the rank and its natural conversion with n. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases.

R004.fact: In a one-dimensional ℚ-subspace of ℂ, every nonzero a spans the space, so each nonzero g has the form g=qa for a nonzero rational q. A nonzero finitely generated module has a finite nonempty generating tuple with all entries nonzero.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated.
Multiplication embeds QJ as the rational span of J.
That space has dimension one.

R004.justification: The single nonzero vector a is independent over ℚ and hence is a basis in dimension one; the coordinate of a nonzero g cannot be zero. Removing zero elements from a finite generating family preserves its span, and an empty remaining family would generate only the zero module, contrary to nonzeroness.

R004.fact: If p is prime and q∈ℚ is nonzero, then q=p^ηu for some η∈ℤ and u with both numerator and denominator prime to p; consequently u,u⁻¹∈ℤ_(p).

R004.justification: Write q=m/d with nonzero integers m,d. Repeated division by p terminates because absolute values strictly decrease when divisible, giving m=p^αm₀ and d=p^βd₀ with α,β≥0 and p dividing neither m₀ nor d₀. Set η=α−β and u=m₀/d₀. The two denominators d₀,m₀ show that u and u⁻¹ lie in R. These powers are in ℚ⊂ℂ, so even negative exponents are defined and nonzero. The finite minimum argument and the two module inclusions are already proved in S004.

R005.justification: The tensor product is generated by pure tensors modulo additivity and balancing relations. For an R-linear A, A(pu)=pA(u), giving a quotient operator and the same compatibility on quotient generators.

Every factor 1,...,r is consequently nonzero; a finite product of nonzero field elements is nonzero. For a unit t with inverse s, kappa(t)kappa(s)=1, so kappa(t) is invertible and cannot be zero in a field.

source_steps.text: H002 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We establish the lowering-power identities by simultaneous induction on t≥0. At t=0, H004 gives hv=λv and xv=0. In the induction step assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v when t≥1, with xv=0 when t=0. The commutators of H003 give h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Also x y^(t+1)v=(yx+h)y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. For t=0 the yxv term is zero directly, and the same coefficient formula holds. Discharge L1 and apply induction: both identities hold for every t in their stated ranges.

For i∈I, iterate the x identity of F001 to obtain x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the empty product is one and the vector is v. If i>0, all factors λ,λ−1,…,λ−i+1 are positive integers; the coefficient and i! are nonzero in ℂ. Since v≠0 by H004, y^i v≠0, hence e_i≠0. F001 also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

To check independence, take arbitrary coefficients c and assume L2: ∑_{k∈I}c_k e_k=0. For any j∈I apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). By F002 this yields c_j[∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)]e_j=0. Each factor is a nonzero complex integer, and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L2 proves linear independence. There are n vectors by F001 and dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n by H003; a linearly independent family of this size is a basis. Thus (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V.

Set z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Expand z in the basis F003. For every coordinate i∈I, its coefficient is annihilated by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is zero, so z=0. All higher y powers of v vanish by applying further y powers. Division by i! in F001 now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

Iterating the formulas in F004 and dividing by r! gives, for every natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i, and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ. The coefficients are the successive products (λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r! and (i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!, respectively, hence the displayed integer binomial coefficients; when r=0 both products are one. If r>i then the x string reaches xe_0=0; if i+r>λ then the y string reaches ye_λ=0. Thus both out-of-range expressions are zero. Together with F001–F004 these are all the asserted coordinate and basis formulas.

Use N001 and H002 to count |I|=n. By H005 choose an integer basis m of M which is also a complex basis of V; its cardinality is n since the e basis of N001 has n elements. Tensoring the integer coordinate isomorphism with R gives R-coordinates on M_R: finite sums ∑_{i∈I}r_i⊗m_i have unique coefficients r_i∈R. Explicitly the coordinate homomorphisms of M extend to these coordinates, and the sum map is their inverse. Under iota these basis tensors go to m_i, still complex-linearly independent, so iota is injective. This proves freeness of rank n and shows its image spans V over ℂ. Admissibility H005 gives preservation of M by every X_r,Y_r; extension by R gives preservation of M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve them; h=xy−yx by H003 preserves them too.

Fix i,j∈I. Evaluate using N001. X_λ kills e_k for k<λ and takes e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Therefore Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ. Also X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ. In Pi Y_(λ−j), an input e_k with kj goes past the end and is zero. At k=j the coefficient is binom(λ,j); hence Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ

Compose the identities F002. On the e basis, E_iλ E_λj=E_ij; thus E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F001, and the scalar inverse belongs to R by F002. Consequently E_ij preserves M_R for all i,j. Together with F001 and F002 these are the asserted lattice and matrix-unit identities. This reasoning has used distinct complex weights only in N001 and makes no assertion about distinct weights modulo p.

By H001 the coefficient ring R is defined, and by H002 the index 0 belongs to I. For arbitrary i,j∈I, E_ii sends iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i: its output is an i-coordinate in M_R, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. For any c∈J_j, the preserving map E_ij of N002 sends c e_j to c e_i, so c∈J_i. Interchanging i and j gives J_i=J_j. Thus all these R-submodules equal J=J_0.

For arbitrary u∈M_R, choose its coordinates d using the e basis N001: iota(u)=∑_{k∈I}d_k e_k. Applying E_ii and N002 gives d_i e_i∈iota(M_R), so d_i∈J_i=J by F001. Conversely every c e_i with c∈J lies in iota(M_R), and the submodule is closed under finite sums. Independence of the e basis makes these expressions unique. Consequently the sum-of-coordinates map ∏_{k∈I}J→iota(M_R) is an R-linear bijection, with inverse the coordinate projections, and M_R=⊕_{k∈I}J e_k after the injective identification iota of N002.

By N002, M_R has n generators over R. The image of these generators under E_ii generates J e_i by F001. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication c↦c e_i is an R-linear isomorphism J→J e_i, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: otherwise F002 would give M_R=0, whose complex span is zero, contrary to N002 and the nonempty basis of V in N001. Thus F001 and F002 give the full common-module and direct-sum assertions.

Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the images 1⊗c0 of a finite generating set of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. The multiplication map is given on pure tensors by ρ⊗c0↦ρc0∈ℂ, with ρ∈ℚ and c0∈J; it is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of R⊂ℚ (H001), a common nonzero denominator in R combines any finite tensor sum into d0^(-1)⊗c0 with 0≠d0∈R and c0∈J. The image of such an expression is c0/d0; a zero image implies c0=0 and hence a zero tensor. Thus multiplication is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (gamma_i), the map sends ρ⊗(∑_{i∈I}gamma_i e_i) to (ρ⊗gamma_i)_{i∈I}; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

By H001, every integer prime to p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. The formula defining kappa:R→K is independent of fractional representatives by cross multiplication, preserves addition and multiplication, and extends the integer map. The balanced tensor maps V_K=M⊗_ℤ K→M_R⊗_R K and back are m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c and (s⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗kappa(s)c. The tensor relations show that both are well-defined; the two composites fix pure tensors, hence are identity maps. Thus they are inverse K-linear isomorphisms. Since the maps act only on scalar factors, they intertwine every operator preserving M, including x,y,h,X_r,Y_r by N002.

The reduction homomorphism R→F_p sends an integer fraction to numerator times inverse denominator. It is surjective because integers already map onto F_p. Its kernel is pR: a reduced fraction maps to zero exactly when its numerator is divisible by p, and division of that numerator by p stays in R. Consequently R/pR≅F_p and M_R/pM_R is an F_p-module. The maps M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K and back send u⊗c to [u]⊗c and [u]⊗c to u⊗c. Changing u by a multiple of p changes u⊗c by zero, since p=0 in K. These formulas are balanced for the quotient R-action, are independent of representatives, and are inverse on pure tensors. They give the second K-linear isomorphism and commute with all induced lattice operators. Combine with F001 to obtain both tensor identifications asserted in the output.

Scalar extension of its coordinate maps gives a K-basis: every pure tensor has its finite coordinate expansion in beta_i, and the extended coordinate maps take beta_i to the corresponding coordinate unit vectors, proving independence. Therefore dim_K V_K=|I|=n=λ+1>0 by N001 and H002. Applying N001 to b e_i and using the tensor isomorphisms gives x beta_0=0, x beta_i=(λ−i+1)beta_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<λ, y beta_λ=0; h beta_i=(λ−2i)beta_i. All coefficients are the integer images in K. This proves the required basis and its generator matrices.

Closure under x,y implies closure under their nonnegative powers. The divided-power indices in T_ij are λ−i,λ,λ−j, all within 0,…,λ; N005 identifies the corresponding X,Y with scalar multiples of those powers. A linear subspace is closed under scalar multiplication and compositions of preserving maps, so W is invariant under every T_ij.
In the zero case temporarily assume L2: W={0}. Then the desired disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately. Discharge L2 to obtain the implication for this case.

For the other case assume L3: W≠{0}. A nonzero subspace contains a nonzero vector, and the beta basis of N005 expands any such vector uniquely. Its coefficients cannot all be zero. Thus there exist a vector w∈W, a coefficient family c∈K^I and an index j∈I with w=∑_{k∈I}c_k beta_k, w≠0 and c_j≠0. Record this compatible joint existence before choosing the witnesses.

Choose compatible w,c,j as in F003. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit action of N005 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. By F001 this vector belongs to W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives beta_i∈W. This holds for every i; since beta is a K-basis, W=V_K. No chosen vector or coordinate is present in that conclusion. Discharge L3 to obtain: if W≠{0}, then W=V_K.

Classical case elimination on W={0} or W≠{0}, using F002 and F004, gives W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W: every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V_K. N005 also gives dim_K V_K=λ+1>0, so V_K is nonzero. By H003 and the definition of L_K, x,y,h span its lattice-induced action; invariance under those generators is equivalent to L_K-invariance. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. H001 and H002 give characteristic p and 0≤λ

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace SL2Reduction
abbrev Index (lam : ℤ) := Fin (lam.toNat + 1)
def localRing (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)}
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := ↥(localRing p)
instance complexAlgebra (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  ((algebraMap ℚ ℂ).comp (localRing p).val.toRingHom).toAlgebra
instance ratComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance (priority := 50) localModule (p : ℕ) : Module (R p) V := Module.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
instance (priority := 50) localTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.restrictScalars (R p) ℂ V
def divided (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := R p ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def localizedImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Submodule (R p) V :=
  (iota p M).range
def Ji (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  (localizedImage p M).comap ((LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ V (e y v i)).restrictScalars (R p))
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) := Ji p M y v 0
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
  (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  (J p M y v).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ

def Preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : M, f (m : V) ∈ M
def RPreserves (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ localizedImage p M, f u ∈ localizedImage p M
structure LatticeOps (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  x : Module.End ℤ M
  y : Module.End ℤ M
  h : Module.End ℤ M
  X : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  Y : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
def Agrees (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (a : LatticeOps M) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : M, (a.x m : V) = x (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.y m : V) = y (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ m : M, (a.h m : V) = h (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.X r m : V) = divided x r (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ r (m : M), (a.Y r m : V) = divided y r (m : V))
def Invariant {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (W : Submodule F U) (f : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ W, f u ∈ W
def Simple {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial U ∧ ∀ W : Submodule F U,
    Invariant W x → Invariant W y → Invariant W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
def Highest (lam : ℤ) (x h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (lam : ℂ) • w
def Admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (c : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (b i : V) = c i) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r)
def extendFamily {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (i : ℕ) : U :=
  if hi : i < lam.toNat + 1 then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def GeneratorFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (x y h : Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Index lam,
    x (b i) = (if i.val = 0 then 0 else
      (((lam - (i.val : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - 1))) ∧
    y (b i) = ((i.val + 1 : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + 1) ∧
    h (b i) = (((lam - 2 * (i.val : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • b i)
def DividedFormulas {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (b : Index lam → U) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Index lam) (r : ℕ),
    X r (b i) = (if r ≤ i.val then
      ((Nat.choose (lam.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val - r)
      else 0) ∧
    Y r (b i) = ((Nat.choose (i.val + r) r : ℕ) : F) • extendFamily (F := F) lam b (i.val + r)
def E (lam : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def MatrixWord {F U : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup U] [Module F U]
    (lam : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F U) (i j : Index lam) : Module.End F U :=
  ((Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹) •
    (X (lam.toNat - i.val) * (Y lam.toNat * X lam.toNat) * Y (lam.toNat - j.val))
def BasisLift (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M),
    ∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val
def Principal (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  b ≠ 0 ∧ J p M y v = Submodule.span (R p) {b}
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a ∧
    Simple (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)


def Lowering (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ℕ,
    h ((y ^ t) v) = (((lam - 2 * (t : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
    x ((y ^ (t + 1)) v) =
      (((((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * (lam - (t : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℂ) • (y ^ t) v)
def CoordinateCore (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∃ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, lam.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) x y h
def Coordinates (lam : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ((lam.toNat + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = lam + 1 ∧
  0 < lam.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Index lam) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
  Lowering lam x y h v ∧
  (∀ i : Index lam, e y v i.val ≠ 0) ∧
  CoordinateCore lam x y h v ∧
  DividedFormulas lam (fun i : Index lam => e y v i.val) (divided x) (divided y)
def LocalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  (iota p M).range = Submodule.span (R p) (M : Set V) ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (localizedImage p M : Set V) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ r, Preserves M (divided x r) ∧ Preserves M (divided y r) ∧
    RPreserves p M (divided x r) ∧ RPreserves p M (divided y r)) ∧
  Preserves M x ∧ Preserves M y ∧ Preserves M h ∧
  RPreserves p M x ∧ RPreserves p M y ∧ RPreserves p M h ∧
  ∃ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a
def MatrixIdentities (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Module.Basis (Index lam) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Index lam,
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    divided x (lam.toNat - i.val) * (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) =
      E lam b i (Fin.last lam.toNat) ∧
    (divided y lam.toNat * divided x lam.toNat) * divided y (lam.toNat - j.val) =
      (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℂ) • E lam b (Fin.last lam.toNat) j ∧
    (∃ c : R p, (c : ℚ) = (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : ℚ) ∧ IsUnit c) ∧
    E lam b i j = MatrixWord lam (divided x) (divided y) i j ∧
    RPreserves p M (E lam b i j)
def CommonModule (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Index lam, Ji p M y v i.val = J p M y v) ∧
  Nontrivial (J p M y v) ∧ Module.Finite (R p) (J p M y v) ∧
  ∃ c : (Index lam → J p M y v) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M,
    ∀ g, iota p M (c g) = ∑ i : Index lam, (g i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def RationalLine (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (qmul p M y v) ∧
  (qmul p M y v).range = Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v : Set ℂ) ∧
  Module.Finite ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J p M y v) = 1
def PrincipalLattice (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  RationalLine p M y v ∧ (∃ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b) ∧
  ∀ b : ℂ, Principal p M y v b → BasisLift p lam M y v b
def TensorMaps (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (hp : CharP K p) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (kap : R p →+* K) : Prop :=
  letI : CharP K p := hp
  letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
  letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
    (psi : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), psi (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) =
      c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] (ModN.mkQ p u)) ∧
    (∀ (f : Module.End ℤ M) (z : VK K M),
      phi (f.baseChange K z) = (f.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K (phi z)) ∧
    (∀ f : Module.End (R p) (MR p M),
      ∃ fbar : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
        (∀ u, fbar (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f u)) ∧
        ∀ z, psi (f.baseChange K z) = fbar.baseChange K (psi z))
def ScalarReduction (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (hp : CharP K p) (kap : R p →+* K),
    (∀ (r : R p) (a b : ℤ), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ) → kap r = (a : K) / (b : K)) ∧
    TensorMaps p K hp M kap
def ReducedBasis (p : ℕ) (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
  ∃ (beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M)) (b : ℂ),
    Principal p M y v b ∧
    (∃ (kap : R p →+* K),
      letI : Algebra (R p) K := kap.toAlgebra
      ∃ (phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M))
        (c : Module.Basis (Index lam) (R p) (MR p M)),
        (∀ (s : K) (m : M), phi (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = s ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
        (∀ i, iota p M (c i) = b • e y v i.val) ∧
        ∀ i, phi (beta i) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R p] (c i)) ∧
    Module.finrank K (VK K M) = lam.toNat + 1 ∧
    GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K)
def ReducedUnits (lam : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  (∀ j : Index lam, (Nat.choose lam.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0) ∧
  ∀ a : LatticeOps M, Agrees M x y h a →
    (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ lam.toNat →
      (a.X r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.x.baseChange K) ^ r ∧
      (a.Y r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (a.y.baseChange K) ^ r) ∧
    ∀ beta : Module.Basis (Index lam) K (VK K M),
      GeneratorFormulas lam (fun i => beta i) (a.x.baseChange K) (a.y.baseChange K) (a.h.baseChange K) →
      ∀ i j k : Index lam,
        MatrixWord lam (fun r => (a.X r).baseChange K) (fun r => (a.Y r).baseChange K) i j (beta k) =
          if j = k then beta i else 0

end SL2Reduction
open SL2Reduction

premises.statement: p is a prime number and K has characteristic p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.
premises.type: Module.Finite ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = (lam + 1).toNat ∧ h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧ h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧ x * y - y * x = h ∧ Highest lam x h ∧ Simple x y h

premises.statement: v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.
premises.type: v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v

premises.statement: M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: a free abelian subgroup admitting an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice assumption is imposed.

P.explanation: For arbitrary prime p, arbitrary field K with CharP K p, integer 0≤λ<p, the given finite-dimensional complex irreducible highest-weight module and vector, and any admissible lattice M, H001–H005 encode the original hypotheses. The three endomorphisms give the Chevalley action through the relations [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h; their invariant complex subspaces are exactly the sl₂-submodules, so Highest plus Simple describes the stated irreducible highest-weight module. H005 asserts the original integer/complex basis condition and all divided-power stability, equivalently U_Z-stability. There is no minimal-lattice assumption. Tensor commutation m⊗c↦c⊗m identifies source M⊗ℤK with VK; its inverse swaps factors and it intertwines all extended lattice operators. Target existentially constructs their restrictions a, requiring Agrees on every m∈M, so each restriction is unique and is the original lattice action. Conversely the original induced action supplies such a. Simple explicitly says Nontrivial VK and universally quantifies every K-submodule W with the three invariance hypotheses and conclusion W=⊥ or W=⊤. This is equivalent to the whole stated target because the three abstract Chevalley generators span L(K), including at p=2. No distinct reduced weights, algebraic closure, or positive λ is assumed; λ=0 remains allowed. Restriction existence is already a derived N002 obligation, not a new premise.

conclusion.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.
conclusion.type: Target K M x y h

representation: V is an arbitrary complex vector space and x,y,h are its complex-linear Chevalley actions. H003 retains finite dimension, all three commutators, a highest vector of weight λ and irreducibility under the generating actions; this is the operator presentation of the given sl₂-module, with the specified v retained separately in H004. λ remains an integer. Under H002, Index λ = Fin(λ.toNat+1) identifies bijectively with {i∈ℤ | 0≤i≤λ}; natural differences are used only inside this range. M is a ℤ-submodule of V; H005 supplies an arbitrary integer basis that is also a complex basis, and stability under every divided power. R is the ℤ-subalgebra of ℚ generated by the displayed prime-to-p fractions, with its exact original carrier established by T005; it is not assumed to be the whole ℚ. MR=R⊗ℤM and iota is the actual scalar multiplication lift; identifying with its image is justified only by N002. J_i and J are preimages of that image under c↦c e_i. qmul is the actual multiplication map ℚ⊗R J→ℂ. Scalar-first VK=K⊗ℤM is the same source tensor construction with factors swapped; T014 uses this convention throughout. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the image of multiplication by p. LatticeOps carries the actual restrictions, and Agrees specifies each value, rather than adding any action assumption. The target constructs these unique restrictions and states nonzero VK and every K-submodule invariant under x,y,h is bottom or top. Proposition-valued definitions only package displayed obligations; none proves them. Endomorphism multiplication is composition, integer coefficients are cast to the indicated field, and all factorials/choose arguments are natural numbers. Inspected pinned APIs: CharP K p asserts exactly (n:K)=0 iff p divides n, rather than merely p·1=0. Module.End multiplication is f.comp g, and Basis.coord is the coefficient function from its finitely-supported coordinate equivalence. LinearMap.liftBaseChange sends s⊗m to s•f(m), while LinearMap.baseChange sends s⊗m to s⊗f(m). ModN is the quotient by the range of the integer-linear p-multiplication map and its ZMod-module instance is canonical. ZMod.algebra is explicitly installed under CharP; the R-action on K is explicitly the one supplied by κ.toAlgebra. Scalar towers for R⊂ℚ⊂ℂ and R⊂ℂ acting on V use those actual inclusion maps. The two finrank theorems require strong rank condition; here R is a subring of ℚ and ℚ is a field, so these are consequences, not extra parameters.

review.disclosure: Unreviewed candidate: only syntax/types and source boundaries are checked here. Normal entry requires actual independent pre-freeze semantic acceptance; the legacy pending field grants none.
